description: Runtime egress probe matrix for the fork's hard requirement: no outbound connection may originate from the harness except model inference, web search/fetch, and MCP servers the repository owner configured.

instrumentation.note: The shim is injected through NODE_OPTIONS and re-propagates itself, so Node child processes are intercepted too. Control probes prove the injection path, the classification, the violation pipeline, and child coverage before any profile probe runs.

allowPolicy.note: The allowlist is empty by default and the repository itself admits nothing: there is no provider host, no wildcard, and no blanket pattern here. A destination is admitted only when the repository owner names it explicitly, either in a probe's allowHosts or at run time through ownerAllow.env. With the env var unset and every probe at allowHosts: [], the number of permitted hosts is exactly zero, which is what the keyless probes assert; a probe that declares a non-empty allowHosts while the owner configured nothing is reported as status=error, and a bare * in the owner configuration is rejected outright.

ownerAllow.blanketPatternNote: A bare `*` host is rejected outright: an allow-everything entry would make this gate meaningless. A scoped pattern such as *.example.invalid is accepted because the owner named that domain.

admittedPurposes: model inference, web search/fetch, and owner-configured MCP servers are the only permitted outbound purposes; none of them is admitted unless the owner configures its destination

probes.description: Trivial Node process started with the gate's NODE_OPTIONS injection; must produce a heartbeat naming this shim, with the recorder enabled and every required layer installed. Without it the gate's injection path is unproven.

Deliberate attempts from the probed process, a worker thread, and a spawned child: a closed loopback port (must be recorded and classified local, and must really be refused by the kernel), reserved external-looking addresses (must be recorded, classified egress, and flagged by the violation pipeline), a request through the repository's own undici dependency (must be recorded by the dispatcher layer, not only by the net layer underneath it), a connect inside a worker thread (proves the shim preloads itself into workers the harness constructs with an empty execArgv), and a reserved DNS name (must be recorded).
Boots the shipped headless profile (base + headless bundles) from source through tsx and prints the headless app's own help, which requires the app plugin to be mounted. Keyless.
Boots the shipped headless profile and runs one task with no API key: the run must reach the credential check, fail loud on the missing key, and make no outbound attempt at all.

output.label: the run reached the credential check and reported the missing key

probes.description: Boots the shipped web profile (base + web-app bundles) from source and serves the Web host on an OS-assigned loopback port; the gate stops it with SIGTERM after the liveness window. Keyless.
Boots the shipped acp profile (base + acp-app bundles) from source and prints its own help. Keyless.
Boots the shipped sdk profile (base + sdk-app bundles) from source and prints its own help. Keyless.
Boots the shipped sdk-minimal profile (sdk-minimal bundle only) from source and prints its own help. Keyless.

skippedProbes.reason: the desktop profile is owned by the Electron application and `dsh --profile desktop` is rejected by the launcher; an Electron main process cannot boot headless in this gate, so the desktop main process egress surface is NOT proved here
the base bundle is a composition layer with no app plugin: `--profile base` would mount and idle with nothing to terminate. Its surface is covered by every profile probe that starts from base

knownLimitations: A non-Node child process (curl, git, ssh, a native binary) cannot be intercepted from inside this process. The shim records its command line as a spawn record so the gate can see it, but kernel-level proof for such a child needs an OS network sandbox instead.
Interception records prove what the harness attempted in JavaScript at the moment of the call, before the connection completes. They are not a packet capture.

NODE_OPTIONS propagation covers Node children, and worker threads are covered by preloading this same shim with --require (Node honors --require but ignores --import in a worker's execArgv). A process that loads the shim by neither route is invisible to this gate; the shim-load and self-check control probes prove both routes.

A worker that runs with a sanitized environment omits DSH_FORK_EGRESS_LOG and records nothing; its shim says so on stderr, and the gate reports the missing expected record as status=error rather than a pass.

A closing port race can reuse the loopback port the self-check reserved; the control still proves the interception because the record is written at call time, and the ECONNREFUSED assertion fails loud if the port was taken.

The gate observes attempts and admits only what the owner explicitly configured, so it cannot certify a destination as permitted by inspecting it. The allowlist is empty in this repository, which is why every keyless probe expects exactly zero egress.
